public_rationale: Two parts can be checked. The first is that chapter 5 of the 2001 book raised a risk of neural networks losing track of facts. The second is that neural systems were still producing false content when the post appeared in February 2023. A third-party preprint says chapter 5 argued that minds must tell specific individuals apart from kinds. It says Marcus held that 'many-nodes-per-variable encodings collapse the distinction' (e1). That fits Marcus's description of a risk of blurring facts about particular things. A survey first posted in February 2022 says deep-learning text generation 'is prone to hallucinate unintended text' (e2). On 9 February 2023, NPR reported that Google's Bard chatbot made a factual error in its first demo (e3). The 'blithely assume' sentence is argument, so it is not scored. The claim is supported on the plain reading. That reading treats the 2001 risk about individuals as an early form of what is now called hallucination.
limitations: The 2001 book was about cognitive models, not chatbots or text generators. Treating its risk as 'hallucination' is an interpretation.

The evidence on persistence comes from 2022 and 2023. The packet has nothing on neural networks producing false content between 2001 and 2021, so it does not show the problem continued through the whole period.
The chapter 5 summary comes from a 2026 preprint, not from a contemporary review of the book.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The hallucination problem in neural networks has persisted since 2001, so assuming it will soon go away ignores 20 years of history.

Plain reading: (a) chapter 5 of the 2001 book raised this risk for neural networks, and (b) neural networks producing false content was still a documented problem up to the post date.
The sentence 'To blithely assume...' is argument, not a checkable fact. It is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: A source other than Marcus shows that chapter 5 of The Algebraic Mind argued neural networks blur facts about individuals. Sources up to February 2023 show that neural text generators still produced false content.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Chapter 5 dealt with an unrelated topic, or neural generation systems had stopped hallucinating before February 2023.
